paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “It is believed that teachers can exert a profound influence on their students’ academic pursuit and personal development.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，你有 30 分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“人们相信教师可以对学生的学术追求和个人发展产生深远的影响。”您可以发表评论、引用示例或利用您的个人经历来完善您的论文。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您应该复制论文开头引号中给出的句子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear two long conversations. At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions. Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将听到两个长对话。在每次对话结束时，您都会听到四个问题。对话和问题都只会说一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A、B、C 和 D 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答题纸 1 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 1 至 4 基于您刚刚听到的对话。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 5 至 8 基于您刚刚听到的对话。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear two passages. At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions. Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将听到两个段落。在每段文章的结尾，你会听到三到四个问题。短文和问题都只会说一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A、B、C 和 D 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答题纸 1 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 9 至 11 题是根据您刚刚听到的段落提出的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 12 至 15 题是基于您刚刚听到的段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks followed by three or four questions. The recordings will be played only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本部分中，您将听到三段讲座或演讲的录音，然后是三到四个问题。录音只会播放一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A、B、C 和 D 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答题纸 1 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 16 至 18 题是基于您刚刚听到的录音。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 19 至 21 题是基于您刚刚听到的录音。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 22 至 25 题是基于您刚刚听到的录音。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: We humans love to believe we are special, but science and technology have repeatedly proved this conviction wrong. People 26 thought that humans were the only animals to use tools, to form teams or to propagate culture, but science has shown that other animals do each of these things.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们人类喜欢相信自己是特别的，但科学和技术一再证明这种信念是错误的。人们曾经认为人类是唯一会使用工具、组建团队或传播文化的动物，但科学表明其他动物也能做这些事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: Meanwhile, technology has quashed (使无效)，one by one, claims that 27 tasks require a human brain. The first adding machine was invented in 1623. This past year, a computer-generated work won an art contest. I believe the moment when computers meet and 28 human intelligence is on the horizon.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与此同时，技术已经一一推翻了认知任务需要人脑的说法。第一台加法机于 1623 年发明。去年，一件计算机生成的作品赢得了一场艺术竞赛。我相信计算机满足并超越人类智能的时刻即将到来。

paragraphs.sourceText: How will human intelligence and creativity be valued when machines become smarter and more creative than the brightest people? There will likely be a spectrum. In some 29 , people still value humans doing things, even if a computer can do it better. It’s been a quarter of a century since a computer beat world champion Garry Kasparov, but human chess hasn’t gone away.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当机器变得比最聪明的人更聪明、更有创造力时，人类的智慧和创造力将如何被重视？可能会有一个频谱。在某些领域，人们仍然重视人类做事，即使计算机可以做得更好。计算机击败世界冠军加里·卡斯帕罗夫已经过去了四分之一个世纪，但人类国际象棋并没有消失。

paragraphs.sourceText: In other fields, human skill will seem costly and 30 . Take illustration for example: most readers don’t care whether the graphic 31 a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer — they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps 32 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 在其他领域，人类技能似乎成本高昂且多余。以插图为例：大多数读者并不关心杂志文章附带的图形是由人还是计算机绘制的 - 他们只是希望它具有相关性、新颖性并且可能具有娱乐性。

paragraphs.sourceText: And, of course, this question isn’t black or white. Many fields will be a 33 , where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers, like in manufacturing today, where much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to 34 the machines.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，这个问题并不是非黑即白的。许多领域将是混合体，一些人找到了一个幸运的地方，但大部分工作是由计算机完成的，就像今天的制造业，大部分工作是由机器人完成的，但必须有人在那里监督机器。

paragraphs.sourceText: If history is any guide, it’s almost certain that advances in AI will cause more jobs to 35 , that creative workers with human-only skills will become richer but fewer in number, and that those who own creative technology will become the new ultra-rich.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果以史为鉴的话，几乎可以肯定的是，人工智能的进步将导致更多工作岗位消失，拥有人类独有技能的创意工作者将变得更加富有，但数量更少，而那些拥有创意技术的人将成为新的超级富豪。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Do You Know When to Quit Wisely?
paragraphs.translationZh: 您知道何时明智地戒烟吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Projects, relationships, and jobs don’t always work out as planned — and it’s not always clear when to give up. We’ve all repeatedly heard the saying that “quitters never win”, but sometimes the best decision is to cut our losses.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 项目、人际关系和工作并不总是按计划进行——而且并不总是清楚何时放弃。我们都反复听过“放弃者永远不会胜利”这句话，但有时最好的决定就是减少损失。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Think about that relationship you held on to even after it had run its course or the job you stayed in despite your boss making you miserable. Many of us try to hold onto the last ray of hope, thinking we can make it work, whatever “it” is. And while perseverance is generally an excellent quality, it may also incline you to over-invest in something that is no longer a good idea.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 想一想即使在它已经走到尽头之后你仍然坚持的那种关系，或者尽管你的老板让你很痛苦你仍然坚持下去的工作。我们中的许多人都试图抓住最后一丝希望，认为我们可以让它发挥作用，无论“它”是什么。虽然毅力通常是一种优秀的品质，但它也可能会让你过度投资于不再是一个好主意的东西。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) As an executive coach, I work with numerous passionate and hard-working leaders who don’t want to “quit”. But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn’t.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 作为一名高管教练，我与许多充满激情且勤奋的领导者一起工作，他们不想“退出”。但最聪明的领导者会学会辨别过早放弃和坚持不应该坚持的东西之间的区别。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) We are all susceptible to the sunk-cost delusion, an unconscious bias that leads us to persist in an endeavor we have already invested time, effort, or money into — even when abandoning it would be more beneficial. We realize that we can’t get back the resources we’ve given, so we persevere — investing in a project that should be halted, staying in a relationship that should be over, or finishing a book we no longer enjoy and should put down, because we’re already halfway through it. If quitting is “not your thing”, you may be especially susceptible to this bias.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 我们都容易受到沉没成本错觉的影响，这是一种无意识的偏见，导致我们坚持我们已经投入时间、精力或金钱的努力——即使放弃它会更有利。我们意识到我们无法收回我们所给予的资源，所以我们坚持不懈——投资一个应该停止的项目，维持一段应该结束的关系，或者完成一本我们不再喜欢并应该放下的书，因为我们已经读了一半。如果戒烟“不是你的事”，你可能特别容易受到这种偏见的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) The sunk-cost delusion causes us to overly worry about what we’ll lose if we move on and not think enough about the costs of not moving on. To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives. Ask yourself: What might I gain by cutting my losses now? Will you be happier or have time for another (better) opportunity? Then ask yourself: What will it cost me to soldier on? For example, is it possible that you’ll be throwing more good money after what you’ve already lost? Or that you won’t have the energy to capitalize on other promising possibilities?
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 沉没成本错觉使我们过度担心如果我们继续前进会失去什么，而没有充分考虑不继续前进的成本。为了抵消这种偏见，有意识地将你的思维重新集中在收益上，这样你就可以更客观地权衡替代方案。问问自己：现在通过减少损失我可以获得什么？您会更快乐还是有时间接受另一个（更好的）机会？然后问问自己：坚持下去我会付出什么代价？例如，在你已经输掉的钱之后，你是否有可能会投入更多的好钱？或者你没有精力去利用其他有前途的可能性？

paragraphs.sourceText: F) The illusion of control can also interfere with our best judgment, leading us to overestimate our ability to control events and attain a positive outcome. This bias gives us a sense of agency and can promote mental health. However, the bias can also result in escalating commitment to a losing course of action. Especially when combined with an “I’m not a quitter” mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 控制幻觉也会干扰我们的最佳判断，导致我们高估自己控制事件和获得积极结果的能力。这种偏见给了我们一种代理感，可以促进心理健康。然而，这种偏见也可能导致对失败的行动方针的承诺不断升级。尤其是当与“我不是一个放弃者”的心态相结合时，感觉我们对一件事情或一个人比我们拥有更多的控制权，这会让我们在应该退出时面临加倍努力的风险。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what’s in your control and what’s not. Think rigorously. While you may be able to influence other people and various circumstances, you can’t force them to change or go your way.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 为了消除这种偏见，请考虑您的情况，并制作一个简单的两栏列表，列出您可以控制的内容和无法控制的内容。认真思考。虽然你也许能够影响其他人和各种情况，但你不能强迫他们改变或走你的路。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Getting clear on what you can control and what you can’t is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere. With a written list in hand, you can ensure you focus on what you can control and better assess whether your continued efforts are worth the expense. Expending effort and emotion on things you can’t control can be both draining and disempowering.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 明确你可以控制什么和不能控制什么对于做出关于是放弃还是坚持的高质量决定至关重要。有了一份书面清单，您可以确保专注于您可以控制的事情，并更好地评估您的持续努力是否值得。将精力和情感花费在你无法控制的事情上可能会让人筋疲力尽，也让人失去力量。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments. And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 研究表明，人们将他们的自我认同和社会地位与他们的承诺联系起来。因为我们认同我们的承诺，退出承诺可能会让人感觉对我们的身份或地位构成威胁。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Take my client Ryan, a leader at a technology company. Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn’t delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear. As Ryan and I explored whether she should cancel the initiative she’d been leading or continue to persevere, she stated, “The thing is, I’m not a quitter.” This singular, fixed sense of self was clouding her judgment and limiting her choices for action.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 以我的客户 Ryan 为例，他是一家科技公司的领导者。瑞安在一个设计项目上投入了两年的时间和大量的精力，但并没有达到所需的结果，但在付出了一切之后放弃它的想法让她难以承受。当瑞安和我探讨她是否应该取消她一直在领导的倡议还是继续坚持下去时，她说，“问题是，我不是一个半途而废的人。”这种单一、固定的自我意识模糊了她的判断力，限制了她的行动选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Our self-concept and identity are mental concepts that influence our behavior. If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept. To overcome this kind of internal obstacle, recall your other positive traits and personality characteristics. Ask yourself: What additional strengths do I have (or aspire to have) that would be helpful to employ here? For example, when I asked Ryan what other positive qualities from her personality she needed to leverage for decision making, she replied, “Discernment and bravery.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 我们的自我概念和身份是影响我们行为的心理概念。如果你强烈地认为自己不是一个放弃者，那么由于你狭隘而僵化的自我概念，你最终可能会陷入困境。为了克服这种内部障碍，请回忆一下您的其他积极品质和个性特征。问问自己：我有哪些额外的优势（或渴望拥有）对在这里发挥作用有帮助？例如，当我问瑞安需要利用她的性格中哪些其他积极品质来做出决策时，她回答说：“洞察力和勇敢。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Now, examine your situation through the lens of each of these facets of yourself. What does the discerning part of you say? The brave part? Considering your decision through these different characteristics will enable you to see that you have more choices. It’s also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts. But it’s important to think through whose opinions you solicit.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 现在，从你自己的各个方面审视你的处境。你挑剔的部分怎么说？勇敢的部分？通过这些不同的特征来考虑你的决定将使你看到你有更多的选择。寻求外部信息来源也很有帮助，而不是仅仅依靠你的思维和直觉。但重要的是要考虑一下你征求谁的意见。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are. If you’re considering whether to shut down your entrepreneurial venture, for instance, reach out to other founders as opposed to just your business partner. Similarly, if you’re looking for love advice, ask someone removed from the ups and downs of your relationship instead of relying only on your best friend. In all cases, I recommend describing your situation and following up with a question like: “How would you manage this situation?”
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 理想情况下，寻找那些对你的决定投入程度比你少的人。例如，如果您正在考虑是否关闭您的创业企业，请与其他创始人联系，而不仅仅是您的业务合作伙伴。同样，如果你正在寻求爱情建议，请询问那些远离你们关系的起起落落的人，而不是仅仅依赖你最好的朋友。在所有情况下，我建议描述您的情况并跟进这样的问题：“您将如何处理这种情况？”

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating. Sticking with the example of the entrepreneurial venture, numbers are your best friend. Use them to remove yourself from the love you have for this idea and consider your burn rate relative to growth plan, industry growth rates, and other factors that predict start-up success. External sources of information can help you see angles and possibilities you might not have considered.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 或者，你也可以寻找确凿的数据来阐明你在任何你正在考虑的努力中成功的真正机会。继续以创业为例，数字是你最好的朋友。使用它们来消除对这个想法的热爱，并考虑相对于增长计划、行业增长率和其他预测初创企业成功因素的烧钱率。外部信息源可以帮助您看到您可能没有考虑到的角度和可能性。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) When something that seemed so promising at the start doesn’t turn out the way we imagined, we can become overly self-critical. Nobody likes to feel that they’ve made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem. The most effective strategy here is to give yourself a break. Practicing self-compassion increases your resilience (韧性), emotional intelligence, compassion toward others, and can boost your performance as well as help you develop a growth mindset. P. Instead of deliberating and criticizing yourself, focus instead on what you can learn from this situation. For example, Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project. And despite ultimately deciding to drop it, she was still happy she had tried and grateful for what the experience taught her. Q. Undeniably, perseverance can help us succeed. But for your well-being, it’s important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action. While letting go can be difficult, it will free up your time, energy, and mental space to imagine new possibilities and pursue new opportunities.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 当一开始看起来很有希望的事情没有像我们想象的那样发展时，我们可能会变得过度自我批评。没有人喜欢觉得自己做出了错误的决定，特别是如果做出明智的决定是你高度尊重的品质的话。最有效的策略就是让自己休息一下。实行自我同情可以提高你的韧性、情商、对他人的同情心，并可以提高你的表现并帮助你培养成长心态。 P. 不要深思熟虑和批评自己，而要关注你可以从这种情况中学到什么。例如，瑞安认识到她通过领导设计项目培养了各种新技能和领导能力。尽管最终决定放弃，但她仍然很高兴自己尝试过，并感谢这段经历教会了她。问：不可否认，坚持不懈可以帮助我们成功。但为了您的健康，重要的是要学会如何区分过早戒烟和坚持失败的行动。虽然放手可能很困难，但它会释放你的时间、精力和精神空间来想象新的可能性并追求新的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Feeling like they have more control over something or someone than they do, people get more committed to their pursuit when they should give up.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 人们感觉自己对某事或某人比自己有更多的控制权，因此在应该放弃的时候会更加坚定地追求自己的目标。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. If you regard yourself as one who never quits, you may end up trapped in your course of action.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 如果你认为自己是一个永不放弃的人，那么你最终可能会陷入自己的行动方针中。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. One of the author’s clients found it hard to give up a design project, in which she had put in a lot of time and effort.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 作者的一位客户发现很难放弃一个设计项目，她在这个项目中投入了大量的时间和精力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. The author suggests that one should direct their thoughts to the gains of quitting timely so as to move on.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 作者建议，人们应该把注意力集中在及时戒烟的好处上，以便继续前进。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. When making a decision, you’d better ask for opinions of those who have less stake in your decision.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40、做决定时，最好征求那些与你的决定关系较小的人的意见。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. For people associating their identity with their commitments, quitting can feel like their identity is threatened.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 对于将自己的身份与承诺联系在一起的人来说，退出会让人感觉自己的身份受到了威胁。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. People who regard highly the quality of making wise decisions do not feel good when they make a bad one.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 高度重视做出明智决定的人在做出错误决定时不会感觉良好。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. The wisest leaders learn to distinguish between giving up too soon and sticking with something irrationally.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 最明智的领导者学会区分过早放弃和非理性地坚持某件事。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. When people are thinking of an endeavor, they should dig out reliable data that tells them how likely they are to succeed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44.当人们考虑一项努力时，他们应该挖掘出可靠的数据来告诉他们成功的可能性有多大。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Having a clear view of what’s in your control and what’s not is vital to making a good decision regarding whether to give up or stick it out.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 清楚地了解什么是你可以控制的，什么是你不能控制的，这对于做出放弃还是坚持的明智决定至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为相互依存的生物，我们无法独立于他人而繁荣发展。我们喜欢与志同道合、有共同兴趣或也相信我们认真对待的事业的人一起工作。这在我们如何将自己组织成不同的集体群体（例如国家、地区、社区、组织和家庭）中显而易见。

paragraphs.sourceText: Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 你所属的群体是否有强烈的集体意识或共同的信仰？其成员之间是否存在相互依赖？您认为这个群体是您存在的重要组成部分吗？如果你的答案是肯定的，那么你正在经历微观版本的团结。

paragraphs.sourceText: What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: “... a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 什么是团结？字典中最简单的定义是：“……一群人之间的统一意见、感觉、目的或兴趣。”

paragraphs.sourceText: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在我们生活的这个日益多元化的社会中，团结呈现出复杂和多方面的特征，因为它在生活在快速变化的环境中并在复杂的分工中工作的独特个人之间形成了相互依赖的纽带。

paragraphs.sourceText: One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism (社群主义). In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy is sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.
paragraphs.translationZh: 团结的一个方面非常符合社群主义的原则。在这种情况下，个人为了共同利益而放弃自己的利益。然而，它对社会凝聚力和排他性的严格遵守限制了个体差异和偏好的表达和实践。因此，为了维持群体的团结而牺牲了个性和自主性。

paragraphs.sourceText: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.
paragraphs.translationZh: 团结也被视为对极端强调个人主义和选择自由的反应。它违背了不受限制的个人的自由主义理念，他们认为社会是他们自由做出选择并按照对他们有利的方式行事的障碍，而不管这些将如何影响他人。

paragraphs.sourceText: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle. Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other — in recognition that one’s fate is in the fate of the other. It is a bond characterized by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但尽管有很多方面，社会理论家仍将团结视为实现社会秩序和进步的关键因素。他们认为，人类社会要在更加多元化的情况下生存，就需要在差异的基础上形成更多新的纽带。有鉴于此，他们认为真正的团结不仅仅是基于共同利益的肤浅关系。团结不仅仅是对自身利益有多大的战略计算的产物。它不是一个建立在“你我对抗世界”原则之上的排他性课程。相反，它是包容性的，而不是强迫性的。团结一致意味着互相支持和挺身而出——认识到一个人的命运取决于另一个人的命运。它是一种以合作实践为特征的纽带，并通过对他人福祉或共同利益的关心而得到加强。它为保护人类尊严而奋斗，倾听最弱势群体的呼声并采取行动。

paragraphs.translationZh: 46.作者对人类有何评价？

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help. Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others. One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不断提出不必要的建议的人可能是善意的并且真诚地想要提供帮助。其他人这样做可能是出于对影响他人能力的自我价值感。一项研究发现，寻求权力倾向较高的人比倾向相反的人更有可能提供建议。

paragraphs.sourceText: Under the guise (外表) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control. They may not be fully aware of this drive, however.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在无私的幌子下，人们可能会被迫向你提供你不想要的建议，因为这让他们感觉自己很强大或处于掌控之中。然而，他们可能并不完全意识到这种驱动力。

paragraphs.sourceText: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些人也可能表现出一定程度的情绪脆弱，很快就会变得心烦意乱，并且需要很长时间才能平静下来。他们的情绪可能只有在童年时期最强烈的时候才会得到证实，从而鼓励他们对大多数情况下过度的不适做出反应。

paragraphs.sourceText: When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当某人为了让自己感觉更强大而提供建议时，建议的接受者往往会注意到他们的行为中存在潜在的焦虑。在这种情况下，人们很容易对建议提供者作出严厉反应并指责他们操纵他人，但这种方法可能会产生意想不到的结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone’s feelings of self-worth, an outright (直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果提供建议的行为积极促进某人的自我价值感，那么彻底的拒绝可能会被视为一种威胁，从而激活他们的战斗或逃跑反应，可能导致他们加倍寻求认可的行为，或导致更大的冲突。

paragraphs.sourceText: The key is to validate without over-identifying. You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. You had better say something like, “Thanks for the idea. I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration. Can I let you know when I need help in the future?”
paragraphs.translationZh: 关键是要验证而不过度识别。你可以让他们知道你已经听到了他们的声音，并欣赏他们的观点，而不必接受那些可能具有破坏性的叙述，而如果没有他们的帮助，你就无法做到这一点。你最好这样说：“谢谢你的想法。我有自己的计划来处理这个问题，但我真的很欣赏你的观点，并且会考虑它。将来我需要帮助时可以告诉你吗？”

paragraphs.sourceText: If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self-regulate. As uncomfortable as it may make you continuously receiving unwanted advice, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely diffuse much faster.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你在巧妙地设定界限时遇到困难，请优先考虑自己的自我调节能力。尽管这可能会让你不断收到不需要的建议，但如果你能够以同情心回应，情况可能会更快地缓解。

paragraphs.sourceText: Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然主动提供建议通常不是预期的结果，但许多收到建议的人常常会感到压力、被冒犯，或者只是对不受欢迎的建议感到恼火。如果您觉得需要的话，在这方面设定一个界限是完全合理的，并且可以给您带来更高的情感安全感。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual’s underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.
paragraphs.translationZh: 设定界限时最好考虑到个人做事的根本原因，以避免不必要的冲突和更多压力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. What is the finding of one study about people who keep giving unsolicited advice?
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 一项关于不断主动提供建议的人的研究结果是什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. How is the advice giver likely to react to the rejection of their advice?
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 建议提供者对其建议被拒绝可能会有何反应？

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. What should the advice receiver do to avoid unnecessary conflict?
paragraphs.translationZh: 55.建议接收者应该怎样做才能避免不必要的冲突？
